# Bystander Hands-Only CPR and Survival After Cardiac Arrest: Evidence Summary

**Conclusion: The claim is well-supported.** Multiple lines of evidence—large national registries, randomized trials, and meta-analyses—consistently show that bystander hands-only (compression-only) CPR improves survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) compared with no bystander CPR at all.

**Key evidence:**

1. **Swedish national registry data**: An 18-year analysis found bystander CPR rates nearly doubled, hands-only CPR increased six-fold, and survival was roughly doubled for any form of bystander CPR compared with no CPR ([emergency-live.com](https://www.emergency-live.com/health-and-safety/survive-an-ohca-the-american-heart-association-revealed-that-hands-only-cpr-increases-survival-rate/)).

2. **Japanese nationwide cohort study (Circulation, 2012)**: This large population-based study directly compared chest-compression-only CPR, conventional CPR, and no bystander CPR, finding compression-only CPR was at least as effective as conventional CPR and both outperformed no bystander CPR ([ahajournals.org](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.112.109504)).

3. **Meta-analysis (PMC, 2010)**: Dispatcher-assisted compression-only bystander CPR was associated with improved survival after OHCA compared to standard CPR, reinforcing that any bystander action beats none ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2987687/)).

4. **AHA Scientific Statement (Circulation, 2008)**: The American Heart Association's foundational advisory concluded that adults receiving hands-only CPR have similar survival chances to conventional CPR—both markedly better than no CPR—forming the basis for the "Hands-Only CPR" public campaign ([ahajournals.org](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/circulationaha.107.189380)).

**Overall assessment**: The evidence is robust and consistent across registry studies, prospective cohorts, and meta-analyses spanning multiple countries and decades. The scientific consensus supports your claim.
